text:
Megan (Sales): Hey team - after the demo the customer's vendor review asked two quick CAIQ clarifications: (1) who owns the encryption keys across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and (2) whether chat logs persist raw prompts. Can someone confirm so I can send a short artifact to their procurement folks?

Lukas (Security): Short answer: Hosted = Redwood-managed keys by default, but enterprise BYOK is available; Dedicated = configurable to use customer KMS; Private = customer-managed keys. For hosted BYOK we integrate with AWS KMS / GCP KMS and can do HSM-backed keys on request. I'll draft the wording.

Jordan (Solutions Eng): On logs: default for POCs is ephemeral logging (no long-term raw prompt retention). Our standard hosted retention is 30 days unless customer configures otherwise. We can enable zero-retention for initial proofs or export audit logs to the customer's project.

Priya (Customer): Thanks - can you map those answers to the specific CAIQ controls and send a one-page artifact? Our vendor risk team wants a clear mapping and an attestation line.

Lukas (Security): Will do. Draft mapping plan: CAIQ key custody Q -> statement of custody (Hosted: Redwood-managed; BYOK option note); CAIQ logging/retention Q -> retention default + opt-out/ephemeral option; CAIQ access Q -> RBAC + audit logging + separation of roles. I can attach: (A) KMS integration diagram, (B) BYOK workflow, (C) retention config snippet, (D) short attestation for SIG.

Megan (Sales): Also customer asked if Redwood staff can access plaintext when using Redwood-managed keys - need a line for SIG explaining separation of duties and that plaintext isn't retrievable without appropriate auditable actions.

Lukas (Security): Confirmed: runtime decrypt occurs on serving nodes with strict RBAC and recorded audit trails. For BYOK the customer retains key lifecycle control and we never store the plaintext key. I'll include exact wording for the SIG.

Jordan (Solutions Eng): Quick copy block you can paste into CAIQ response: 

```
KMS & Key Custody: Hosted deployments default to Redwood-managed KMS with an enterprise BYOK option. Dedicated and Private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM. Key rotation and access are logged; BYOK keys are controlled by the customer and not stored by Redwood.

Logging & Retention: By default we retain operational logs for 30 days. For POCs we can enable ephemeral logging (no persistent raw prompt retention). Retention and export of audit logs to the customer's cloud project are configurable.

Access Controls: Production access to decrypted data requires RBAC approval and is logged. Separation of duties is enforced; we provide audit artifacts on request.
```

Lukas (Security): I'll also upload the one-pager and attachments to the shared drive and post links here. Also linking our SOC2/encryption controls and the internal BYOK runbook.

Megan (Sales): Perfect. Priya, will that work for your vendor team or do they want additional artifacts (e.g., rotation proof, KMS audit extracts)?

Priya (Customer): Rotation proof would be helpful but not mandatory for initial pass. If you can supply rotation windows and a screenshot of audit logs or the log export workflow, that's ideal.

Lukas (Security): Noted - I'll include a sanitized sample of rotation entries and the export steps. ETA EOD. :thumbsup:

redwood-ops-bot: Uploaded: https://internal.redwood/drive/kms-byoe-diagram.pdf (kms-byoe-diagram.pdf)

Megan (Sales): Thanks everyone - I'll bundle the one-pager + links and send to the vendor team this afternoon.

Lukas (Security): Draft CAIQ mapping + attestation uploaded to: https://internal.redwood/controls/ca iq-mapping-kms-2026.pdf (placeholder). ETA to finalize after review: 18:00 PST.
